mechanism_narrative: The steady recovery in WORKPLACES and the small lift in TRANSIT indicate more weekday movement through the city, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as commuting traffic converts into store visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying at or above -10 and TRANSIT staying at or above -21.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above 11 percent, local substitution keeps consumers closer to home and shifts spending into nearby retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 11 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 14 days after two consecutive weeks with RESIDENTIAL above 11.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops another 2 points from its current low level while WORKPLACES do not improve, access frictions should suppress discretionary shopping trips and push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls > 2 points week-on-week from a level near -20 while WORKPLACES remain below -8
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean even though TRANSIT falls further and WORKPLACES stay below -8.

mechanism_narrative: A short-run rebound in PARKS usually diverts time away from shopping trips in warm-weather or outdoor-oriented weeks, so a further rise in PARKS should hold RETAIL_REC down over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days after a week-on-week PARKS rise of at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of higher GROCERY_PHARM and stable RESIDENTIAL signals neighborhood errand consolidation, which should spill into more nearby retail visits and lift RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its last 4-week mean over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM stays positive and RESIDENTIAL stays above 11.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent gap between weak PARKS and weak TRANSIT means fewer out-of-home discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC should continue drifting down over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to its last 2-week mean over the next 14 days despite PARKS and TRANSIT remaining below -10 and -20 respectively.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stop recovering and slip back below -10, the city is entering a renewed mobility constraint regime that will reduce incidental shopping and depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses below -10 after having been above -10 in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES crosses below -10.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM over one week signals weekend and neighborhood activity clustering, which should precede a small retail uptick within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 7 days after both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM rise week-on-week.
